beats.text: Every night, Seneca sat in judgement of his own day. Five questions he asked himself.
One. What did I do well today? Name it, so the good is deliberate, not accidental.
Two. What did I do badly? Face it plainly, as a friend would — not as an enemy.
Three. What did I leave undone that I should have done?
Four. Where did a feeling — anger, fear, envy — end up running me?
Five. How, precisely, will I be a little better tomorrow?
He slept well, he said, because each night he had already settled his accounts.
